title: Service recovery runbook: customer notes and status templates
content:
Purpose and scope:
This document is a compact, customer-focused runbook for drafting: (1) initial status page updates, (2) follow-up operational updates, and (3) a concise post-incident summary tailored for customers. It is intentionally prescriptive — copy snippets are provided so CS/Support can move quickly.

When to use this runbook:
- Any incident affecting request latency, error rates, model fallback, or API availability that potentially impacts customers’ SLAs or user experience.
- Use for incidents that require a public status page update and a customer-facing postmortem (severity P2 or higher by internal classification).

Audience:
- Customer Success, Support, Technical Account Managers (TAMs), and Product leads handling customer outreach.

How this is organized:
A. Immediate status page template (first 15–60 minutes)
B. Operational follow-up (2–8 hour updates)
C. Customer-facing postmortem summary (1–5 business days)
D. Quick FAQ and recommended customer actions
E. SLI/SLA impact note and credits language
F. Internal handoff checklist for escalation to enterprise/TAMs

A. Immediate status page template (short)
- Title: Service degradation: increased API latency and intermittent errors
- Impact: Some customers experienced increased request latency and intermittent 5xx errors for text generation and chat endpoints in us-west-2.
- Timeline (start): ~2026-12-18T02:10 UTC (ongoing)
- Scope: ~3–7% of requests across a subset of models were affected; most requests remained healthy.
- Customer guidance: We are actively routing traffic to healthy capacity and applying mitigations; no customer action required at this time.
- What we’re doing: Engineering is investigating root cause and applying traffic routing and instance-level mitigations. We will provide an update within one hour.
- Contact: status.redwood.ai and support@redwood.ai for account-specific concerns.

Copy snippet for email/portal (immediate):
Subject: Redwood Inference — Service degradation affecting some generation requests
Body: Hi — We’re investigating increased latency and intermittent errors affecting a small percentage of generation requests in US-West. Our engineers are actively mitigating and routing traffic to healthy instances; we expect to provide a substantial update within the hour. We will follow up with a post-incident summary after the issue is resolved. No action is required on your side right now. — Redwood Support

B. Operational follow-up template (2–8 hours)
- Update header: Ongoing — mitigations in place; investigating root cause
- What changed since last update:
  * Deployed targeted routing rules to divert traffic from affected instance pools.
  * Applied a hotfix to reduce memory pressure on quantized runtime (rollout: 20% -> 60% of affected hosts).
- Current impact: error rate decreased from ~3.5% to ~0.4% over the last 30 minutes; median latency returned to baseline for routed traffic. A small fraction of accounts on Dedicated capacity may still see elevated tail latency.
- Next steps:
  1. Complete hotfix rollout to remaining hosts (ETA 90 minutes).
  2. Run post-deployment validation using synthetic prompt suite.
  3. Begin preparing customer-facing postmortem draft.
- ETA for next update: 60–120 minutes

Operational copy snippet (follow-up):
We have deployed routing controls and a hotfix to affected hosts. Error rates have dropped significantly; we are continuing rollout and validation. For Dedicated customers with persistent elevated latency, TAMs will reach out directly with account-specific mitigations.

C. Customer-facing postmortem summary (concise)
Purpose: Provide customers with a clear, non-technical summary of what happened, why, what we did, impact on customers, and concrete remediation and prevention steps. Keep the tone factual, concise, and accountable.

Template structure (use these sections):
1) Incident snapshot (one paragraph)
2) Customer impact (bullets)
3) Root cause (one-liner + brief explanation)
4) Remediation performed (bullets with times)
5) Preventative actions and timeline (bullets)
6) SLA/credit implications (if any)
7) Contact and follow-up

Example final text (to be adapted per incident):
Incident snapshot: On 2026-12-18 between 02:10–04:45 UTC, Redwood Inference experienced increased latency and intermittent 5xx errors affecting a subset of generation and chat requests served from the us-west-2 region. Redirection and a runtime hotfix reduced error rates and restored median latency for the majority of requests; the incident was mitigated at 04:20 UTC and fully resolved by 04:45 UTC.

Customer impact:
- Affected scope: approximately 3–7% of global generation requests were impacted, concentrated in us-west-2.
- Symptoms: increased tail latency and intermittent 5xx responses; some customers on Dedicated pools saw transient elevated latency.
- Data retention: no user data was lost or exposed. All request/response data handling remained within existing controls.

Root cause (brief): A mis-estimated memory allocation path in the quantized runtime lead to elevated memory pressure under a specific request mix and sequence length distribution, triggering degraded request processing in a subset of hosts.

Remediation performed:
- 02:25 UTC — Enabled traffic routing to healthy capacity to reduce load on affected hosts.
- 02:55 UTC — Deployed a targeted hotfix to the inference runtime reducing memory allocations for long-sequence requests.
- 04:20 UTC — Hotfix rollout complete for production capacity; synthetic checks returned to baseline.
- 04:45 UTC — Monitoring confirms stabilized error rates and latencies across all regions.

Preventative actions:
- Immediate: Add defensive throttles and early-cache bypass for high-memory paths (completed within 72 hours).
- Short-term: Expand synthetic coverage for long-sequence prompts in canary suites (ETA 2 weeks).
- Mid-term: Add memory-usage alerting on per-host quantized runtime (ETA 4 weeks).
- Long-term: Runtime refactor to reduce worst-case memory growth and add automatic fallback to lower-memory model variants (planning Q1 2027).

SLA/credit implications:
- We will evaluate account-level SLO impact and issue credits where customers meet the credit criteria per our SLA policy. TAMs or account support will reach out to affected enterprise customers with proposed credit calculations within 5 business days.

Contact and follow-up:
- For account-specific questions, contact your TAM or support@redwood.ai.
- We will publish a detailed technical RCA to our Confluence and link it from the public status page.

D. Quick FAQ (customer-friendly)
Q: Was any data exposed?
A: No. There is no evidence of data loss or exposure; request handling remained within our normal control plane and logging policies.

Q: Do I need to change my integration or retry logic?
A: No changes necessary. Standard client retry behavior is sufficient. We recommend exponential backoff for high-throughput jobs.

Q: Will this affect model outputs or quality?
A: No change to model weights or intended model behavior. Fallback routing may have served lower-latency model variants for a small percentage of requests; output differences were negligible for most use cases.

E. SLI/SLA impact note (standard wording)
We will measure incident impact against token-level successful-response SLI and per-route latency SLI. Where an account crosses the SLA credit threshold due to this incident, we will propose credit amounts within 5 business days. Please reach out to your TAM for account-specific calculations.

F. Internal handoff checklist for TAMs and Enterprise support
- [ ] Confirm list of impacted enterprise accounts (Support to provide list).
- [ ] Draft tailored outreach email if customers observed business impact.
- [ ] Prepare SLO impact report and proposed credit amounts.
- [ ] Schedule postmortem review with Engineering and SRE; invite customer-facing stakeholders.

Guidance for editing the templates:
- Keep technical jargon minimal in customer-facing copies; include links to the technical RCA for customers that want deeper detail.
- For Dedicated customers, include account-specific mitigation details and any temporary capacity adjustments.
- If a security or data exposure element is discovered, escalate immediately to Security & Compliance and follow the breach communication playbook.

Versioning and ownership:
Owner: Customer Success (Sofia Ramirez)
Operational lead: Marcus Liu (SRE/Infra)
Engineering reviewer: Aisha Patel (Serving runtime)
Last updated: 2026-12-20

Appendix: suggested Slack/Email snippets for TAM outreach- Short Slack DM: "Heads-up: Incident in us-west-2 affected generation latency earlier; mitigations applied and we will follow up with a short RCA. Reaching out to impacted customers now. Let me know if you want me to join any calls."
- Detailed customer email subject: "Redwood Inference post-incident summary — us-west-2 latency (Dec 18)"
- Call script bullets: open, impact summary, mitigation and timeline, next steps, ask for customer questions.

Notes and filing:
- Link final customer-facing summary from the public status page and attach to Confluence RCA.
- Mark this draft as final once engineering confirms timelines and the SLO impact spreadsheet is available.

End of runbook.
